clue.text: Bare-legged, perhaps, avoiding ugly leer of despicable person

definitions.note: a rotter, someone of bad character

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of bare-legged are only one possible arrangement, so they are to be reworked
avoiding says the letters of leer are to be kept out of the rearrangement
ugly says the word leer is spoilt into a jumble, so its letters may come out in any order

explanation.surface: Someone showing bare legs steers clear of a lecherous look from an unpleasant character.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: BARELEGGED (shuffled, as 'perhaps' says) avoids the letters of LEER, jumbled as 'ugly' says; what is left gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a rotten, untrustworthy individual compares them to a spoilt egg.

clue.text: Top copy chased by Times

indicators.note: chased by puts the first piece in front, with the second following it

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper's best imitation is followed up by The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the peak or summit of something is its highest point.

clue.text: Found Basil Faulty in east of France hotel!

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled name inside the French word and the letter that follow it

parts.note: est is the French word for east
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: faulty says the name Basil is broken, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Basil Fawlty, the manic hotelier of the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, turns up running a hotel in eastern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faulty' puns on Fawlty but is the anagram signal: BASIL becomes ABLIS, placed in EST and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to found a business or institution is to set it up.

clue.text: Bereavement between the covers of gay magazine

definitions.note: a noun here, a glossy being a magazine on shiny paper

indicators.note: between says the word for bereavement sits between the two outside letters
the covers of a word are its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: a bereavement is a loss of someone close

explanation.surface: A sad death story printed inside the pages of a gay-interest periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is the everyday name for a magazine printed on shiny, high-quality paper.

clue.text: With right to be called, let it end badly

indicators.note: badly says the words let it end are put together wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a rightful claim insists the matter should not end poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both having a rightful claim and bearing a title or name.

clue.text: Perhaps French camping call centre restricted agreement

parts.note: in a tent, rendered in French, would be en tente, written as one word here

indicators.note: restricted says the word for centre holds the word for call within it

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
to dial is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A French call centre staffed from a campsite keeps a limited deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags a loose French phrasing: 'en tente' means 'in a tent'. DIAL goes into CORE to make the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The name for the 1904 Anglo-French understanding, a friendly diplomatic accord.

clue.text: Record attempt to cover pole in fabric

indicators.note: to cover says the first two pieces wrap round the pole letter

parts.note: to tape something is to record it
a try is an attempt
S is short for the south pole

explanation.surface: Someone tries to set a record by covering a pole with cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven wall-hanging is a heavy decorative textile, so a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Subject to choice, but not quite

indicators.note: not quite says the word for choice stops short of its final letter

parts.note: your pick is your choice

explanation.surface: Something is left to choice, though not entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Regularly repair musical instrument's sound amplifier

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of repair, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: a trumpet is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone routinely fixes the amplifier of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining the pieces. Twinned with 14 across, an identical clue bar its last word.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hearing aid: a horn held to the head to magnify sound for the deaf.

clue.text: Buzzer and horn sound about right for Russian course requirement

parts.note: a bee is a buzzing insect

indicators.note: about says the horn noise goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a toot is the sound of a horn

explanation.surface: An insect and a honking horn noise surround something needed for a Russian lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian course' suggests a language class; it is a course of a meal, borscht, which needs this root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Borscht, the Russian soup course, is made from this red root vegetable.

clue.text: Press ID

definitions.meaning: identity documents, which officials ask to see

explanation.surface: A press card serving as identification.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural covers both newspapers and identity documents in everyday use.

clue.text: Bride can suss out contact information

indicators.note: out says the words are put out of order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bride can work out who someone is from their details.
explanation.definitionFit: A small printed card carrying a person's name, phone number and email.

clue.text: Four in cast mutinied, like Piglet

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: like Piglet means very small

indicators.note: in says the Roman numeral sits inside the jumbled word
cast says the word mutinied is thrown into a new shape

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four members of a cast staged a mutiny, like Piglet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges MUTINIED into DIMINUTE; IV goes into it. Piglet, in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh, is a Very Small Animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Piglet is famously tiny, so like him means very small.

clue.text: Wind and fire wiping out half the network system

indicators.note: half takes the first two letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Wind and fire knock out half the communications network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiping out' is a link here: each word loses its back half.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless local networking, the standard for connecting devices to the internet.

clue.text: Regularly repair musical instrument's sound receivers

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of repair, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: drums are percussion instruments; the 's reads as the plural here

explanation.surface: Someone routinely fixes the receivers on a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Twin of 8 down: same clue, last word changed, and 'instrument's' read loosely as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The membranes inside the ear pick up vibrations, so they receive sound.

clue.text: Proof of wanton tartiness

indicators.note: wanton means unruly, so the letters of tartiness run wild

explanation.surface: Evidence of loose, wanton behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof as a suffix means able to withstand, as in waterproof.

clue.text: Anxious heart of Putin: his currency finally devalued

indicators.note: heart of takes the central letter of Putin

parts.note: the rouble is Russia's currency

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of devalued

explanation.surface: Putin is worried at heart because his money has lost value.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: worried, uneasy, disturbed in mind.

clue.text: Success with other arrangement so far

parts.note: a hit is a success

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of other are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A hit song, made with a fresh arrangement, has done well up to now.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: until now, up to this point in time.

clue.text: Bias of south-facing gardens

indicators.note: facing puts the south letter in front of the gardens

parts.note: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: Gardens laid out to face south have a slant.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW Gardens is London's famous botanical garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to slant or distort, as in skewing statistics.

clue.text: Southwestern enterprise zone vacated in allergic response

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so each word keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An enterprise zone in the south-west is abandoned because of allergies.
explanation.walkthrough: An enterprise zone is a UK area given tax breaks to attract business.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay fever, for one, makes you expel air violently through the nose.

clue.text: High on drugs, ruins the environment

indicators.note: high suggests being out of one's head, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting high on drugs is wrecking the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the setting or conditions around something.

clue.text: Man of religion employed by Arab billionaire

indicators.note: employed by says the letters work within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cleric is on the payroll of a rich Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher and leader of a congregation.

clue.text: Type of rock garden looked a mess to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with takes the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A rock garden looked untidy at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock garden' reads as one thing, but 'rock' belongs to the definition, glitzy 1970s pop.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter-laden 1970s pop music, as played by David Bowie and T. Rex.

clue.text: This source of insect sounds almost a type of food

indicators.note: almost says the food word loses its final letter

parts.note: a timbale is a dish baked in a drum-shaped mould

explanation.surface: Something that produces bug noises is nearly a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The vibrating membrane with which a cicada produces its loud song.

clue.text: Willing in the morning to empower

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon
to enable is to empower

explanation.surface: Keen in the morning to give someone authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: compliant, open to persuasion.

clue.text: Once more fire in nerd-like fashion

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A geek, once again, gets sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like dismissal; here it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To set alight again, or to revive a feeling.

clue.text: Internet mob organisation

indicators.note: organisation is arranging, so the letters are put in order anew

parts.note: only the tail of this word, net, is fodder; its front, inter, is split off as the definition

explanation.surface: An online mob gets organised.
explanation.walkthrough: A lift-and-separate: 'Internet' must be split in two, with its front half, meaning bury, standing as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bury a body in a tomb or grave.
